Curriculum › Year 6

Year 6: what your child practises

In Year 6, Sharpwise has 35 topics in maths and 16 topics in English. Each one is below in plain words, with ideas to try at home.

Year 6 topics follow the National Curriculum for England. This page is made from the game's own list of topics, so it changes when the game does.

Play Sharpwise

Maths in Year 6

35 topics, grouped by the part of the curriculum each one practises.

Number: number and place value

Place value to 10 million
Numbers to 10,000,000
Round to a required accuracy
Round to a required degree of accuracy
Negative numbers
Negative numbers, intervals across 0

Try at home:

  • Make numbers from pairs of playing cards and ask which digit stands for tens and which for ones.

Number: addition, subtraction, multiplication and division

Long multiplication
Long multiplication, up to 4 digits × 2 digits
Long and Short Division
Long and short division, interpreting remainders
Mental calculation
Mental, mixed operations, large numbers
Factors, multiples and primes
Common factors, common multiples, primes
Order of Operations
Order of operations and brackets
Multi-step Problems
Multi-step problems, estimating to check

Try at home:

  • Set out egg boxes or muffin trays and count the rows and columns to find the lots of.
  • Share a bowl of grapes fairly between family members and ask how many each, and how many are left.
  • Add the prices of two snacks in your head, then take one away to check the answer.
  • Arrange 12 buttons into equal rows in different ways and see which sizes fit.
  • Hide a number under a cup and give clues, like "it is 3 more than 5", until your child can find it.

Number: fractions (including decimals and percentages)

Simplify and compare fractions
Simplify, common denominators, compare >1
Adding and subtracting fractions
Add/subtract, different denominators, mixed numbers
Multiplying fractions
Multiply proper fractions, simplest form
Dividing fractions
Proper fraction ÷ whole number
Fractions, decimals and percentages
Fraction as division; FDP equivalences
Decimals to 3 places
3 dp place value; ×÷ 10, 100, 1,000
Multiplying decimals
Decimals (≤2 dp) × whole numbers
Dividing to decimals
Division with a 2 dp answer

Try at home:

  • Cut a pizza or an apple into equal parts and ask for one half, one quarter or three quarters.
  • Read prices and measurements aloud: say what the digit after the point means, in tenths or hundredths.

Ratio and proportion

Ratio and scale
Relative sizes, unequal sharing, scale factor
Percentages of amounts
Percentages of amounts, comparison

Try at home:

  • Double or halve a recipe together and talk about how every amount changes by the same rule.
  • Spot sale labels and work out one tenth of the price, then a half or a quarter of it.

Algebra

Using formulae
Simple formulae
Linear sequences
Linear number sequences
Missing numbers with letters
Missing numbers algebraically
Two unknowns
Two unknowns; combinations

Try at home:

  • Hide a number under a cup and give clues, like "it is 3 more than 5", until your child can find it.
  • Count stairs, spoons or steps together, then count backwards, and stop to ask what comes next.

Measurement

Converting Units and Miles
Convert units to 3 dp, miles and kilometres
Same Area, Different Perimeter
Same area, different perimeter; when formulae apply
Area of Triangles and Parallelograms
Area of parallelograms and triangles
Volume of Cuboids
Volume of cubes and cuboids

Try at home:

  • Compare a cup, a jug and a bowl: which holds more? Use a ruler or shoe-lengths to measure the table.

Geometry: properties of shapes

Nets of 3-D Shapes
Describe 3-D shapes and their nets
Missing Angles
Missing angles in shapes, on lines, vertically opposite
Parts of a Circle
Radius, diameter and circumference

Try at home:

  • Go on a shape hunt around the house for circles, boxes, cylinders and right angles.

Geometry: position and direction

Four-Quadrant Coordinates
Describe positions on the full coordinate grid, all four quadrants
Reflect in the Axes
Translate and reflect in the axes

Try at home:

  • Go on a shape hunt around the house for circles, boxes, cylinders and right angles.

Statistics

Pie Charts
Interpret pie charts and use them to solve problems
Line and Conversion Graphs
Interpret line graphs and conversion graphs
The Mean
Calculate and interpret the mean as an average

Try at home:

  • Tally the cars passing the window or the colours of socks, then say which has most and fewest.

English in Year 6

16 topics, grouped by the part of the curriculum each one practises.

Reading: comprehension

Inference
Inferring feelings, thoughts and motives, justified with evidence
Figurative Language
Figurative language

Try at home:

  • After a bedtime story, ask who it was about, what happened and where, then how many or why.
  • Read a few lines together every day and ask your child to point to the tricky words.

Writing: transcription (spelling)

ough and ei Spellings
ough; ei after c
Often-Confused Words
Homophones and often-confused words
Year 5–6 Word List (51–100)
Statutory word list, words 51–100
Spell the missing word
Writing: transcription (spelling)

Try at home:

  • Choose three words a night: look, cover, write, check, and then say what makes each one tricky.

Writing: composition

Tense and Agreement
Consistent tense and subject–verb agreement

Try at home:

  • Look at a favourite book together and spot the full stops, question marks and describing words.

Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation

Formal or Informal
Formal and informal vocabulary and structures
Synonyms and Antonyms
Synonyms and antonyms
Active and Passive
Active and passive
The Subjunctive
Subjunctive forms in formal writing
Linking Paragraphs
Linking adverbials and ellipsis
Semicolons, Colons, Dashes
Semi-colon, colon and dash between independent clauses
Lists and Bullet Points
Colon before a list, semi-colons in lists, bullet points
Hyphens
Hyphens to avoid ambiguity
Subject and Object
Subject and object

Try at home:

  • Choose a word of the day and take turns using it in a sentence, or finding a word that means the same.
  • Look at a favourite book together and spot the full stops, question marks and describing words.
